title: Finite state machine (Mealy and Moore)
summary: A finite state machine (FSM) has states, inputs, outputs, and transitions. Mealy machine: output depends on current state AND input. Moore machine: output depends only on current state. State encoding: binary (minimum bits), one-hot (one bit per state, simpler logic), Gray code (adjacent states differ by one bit, reduces glitches).

structure.meaning: Output = f(state, input). Output can change immediately on input change (faster). More outputs possible.
Output = f(state). Output changes only on state transition (simpler, no glitches). Fewer outputs.
Holds the current state. n = ceil(log2(num_states)) for binary encoding.
Computes next state from current state + inputs.
One bit per state. Simpler next-state logic (fewer gates) but more flip-flops.
Minimum flip-flops but complex next-state logic.
Adjacent states differ by one bit. Reduces glitches in asynchronous outputs.

notes: FSMs are the basis of control units, protocols, and sequential logic.
Mealy machines can have glitches (output changes before clock edge).
Moore machines are safer for synchronous design.
State minimization reduces the number of states (and flip-flops).
FSM design: state diagram -> state table -> state assignment -> logic minimization -> implementation.
